messages:
maggie: Heads up — seeing big p95 east-west latency spikes between GPU hosts during the 11:00-11:10 UTC batching window. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~620ms across several racks for ~6 minutes. :warning:

sre-bot: ALERT: east-west-p95-spike detected (cluster: g-prod, impacted: gpu-pool-3). Auto-page sent to @oncall.

oncall: I'm on it. Maggie, can you paste the perf graphs and which racks/nodes are affected?

maggie: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/?panel=ew-p95
maggie: Affected: rack-r16 (nodes g-16-01..g-16-06) and rack-r17 (g-17-01..g-17-04). Packet drop counters tick up around the same time.

raj: Possible MTU/fragmentation? We recently rolled jumbo frames in r16 last week. Any config drift between TORs?

diego: grabbed tcpdump on g-16-03 during spike, small sample below:
```
08:23:12.345678 IP 10.12.16.3.5000 > 10.12.17.2.5000: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12789, ack 54321, win 4128, length 444
08:23:12.346789 IP 10.12.17.2 > 10.12.16.3: frag 0  mtu 1500
08:23:12.347890 IP 10.12.16.3 > 10.12.17.2: ICMP frag-needed, mtu 9000
```

jen: ICMP frag-needed is a red flag — looks like path MTU blackhole or mismatched MTU on some hop. Did the TOR or leafs get a config rollback?

ops-lead: We had a partial rollback on r17 TORs earlier today to revert a kernel bump. Might have defaulted MTU 1500 on those switches.

raj: That explains fragmentation+retransmits during larger batched RPCs. Batching increases packet sizes (KV cache + payload), so PMTU issues show up only under peak.

diego: Also captured RDMA counters from g-16-03 via rdma-core counters:
```
ib_counters g-16-03:
  retransmit: 340 -> 1200 (spike)
  link_error: 0
  seq_err: 16
```

maggie: Can we confirm TOR config MTU on both r16 and r17? If r16 hosts use 9000 and r17 TOR is 1500, we get ICMP frag-needed and heavy TCP retransmits under big batches.

oncall: I'm SSHing to the TORs now. Running `show interface | include MTU` and `ethtool` on hosts.

k8s-bot: k8s events: pod eviction attempts increased for gpu-pool-3 between 11:02:00 and 11:07:30; autoscaler triggered 4 more nodes.

jen: While oncall checks, can we mitigate quickly? Options: 1) lower batch max-payload to keep packet <1500, 2) temporarily disable jumbo on r16 hosts, 3) divert batch traffic to dedicated path with jumbo consistency. Thoughts?

raj: Fastest is to reduce batch payload to force smaller frames — can toggle at routing-layer config on inference router. But perf hit. Second is to push MTU change to r17 TORs (risky during hours).

maggie: Start with a small config: reduce max_batch_bytes by 30% for gpu-pool-3 for the ongoing window. I'll revert after stabilization.

diego: oncall report: r17-tor-2 had MTU 1500 on internal ML VLAN. r16-tor-1 is 9000. Confirmed mismatch.

oncall: Applied temporary traffic steering to avoid r17 for heap traffic and triggered max_batch_bytes reduction. Monitoring.

sre-bot: NOTE: mitigation change applied by maggie at 11:05 UTC (change-id: cfg-4582).

maggie: After the change p95 dropped back to ~130ms within 90s. Packet retransmit counters decayed.

ops-lead: Good. We'll schedule a coordinated MTU standardization and change window for r17 TORs tonight (low traffic) and update runbook to verify MTU parity after kernel rollbacks.

raj: Follow-ups: create ticket INFRA-3421 for MTU audit across all ML clusters, add automated MTU parity check to host-boot scripts, and add an alert for ICMP frag-needed spikes.

jen: Also add a prompt in deployment playbooks: if you rollback TOR kernel/config, validate `show interface` + `ethtool` parity.

diego: Uploading tcpdumps and rdma counters to the incident folder: s3://incidents/2024-11-09/ew-p95-mtu-mismatch/.

maggie: Thanks everyone. Leaving the reduced batch config in place for 30 minutes then we'll revert if stable. Will follow up with postmortem. :white_check_mark:

ops-lead: Postmortem owner assigned: jen. Target ETA for draft: 48h.

oncall: closing the page. If anyone sees residual anomalies, ping @oncall.

sre-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (auto): east-west-p95-spike resolved after temporary batch reduction and MTU parity fix scheduled.
